description.narrative:
The overall objective of the Gaza Early Recovery Program is to contribute to restoring safe and unimpeded access to basic services through cash assistance and rubble removal.
Through the program, internally displaced non-refugee families will be assisted to find affordable and adequate housing, and at the same time being provided rental subsidies, while awaiting the reconstruction of their destroyed homes.
.....................................................................................................................
Based on the recovery needs highlighted in the revised program document dated 2021.11.11, UNDP is proposing to revise the scope of the Gaza Early Recovery Programme and request additional funding from Sweden (25 MSEK with extension of the activity period until June 2023) in order to address gaps for TSCA for refugee internally displaced households, alongside TSCA provided to non-refugee IDPs; include interventions geared towards restoring and stabilizing the livelihoods of conflict-affected people, namely those who lost their jobs, those who lost their homes and are unemployed, those who lost both, as a result of the hostilities of May 2021.

Med en långvarig närvaro i Palestina har UNDP en djup förståelse av den lokala kontexten. UNDP har ett solitt partnerskap med Palestinska institutioner, med organisationer från det civila samhället och internationella utvecklingspartners, samt med olika delar och nivåer av samhället.
Genom kontantstöd samt säker undanröjning av spillror och byggnadsrester avser Gaza Early Recovery program bidra till att återställa trygg tillgång till grundläggande service. Programmet bistår internt fördrivna familjer (ej flyktingar) med prisvärda och lämpliga bostäder och hyressubventioner medan de väntar på återuppbyggandet av sina förstörda hem. Detta program kommer också att bidra till att skapa kortsiktiga arbetstillfällen för ekonomiskt utsatta människor i Gaza.
Det geografiska fokuset i insatsen kommer vara hela Gaza, om inte annat specificeras i avtalet.
Insatsen föreslås vara 18 månader lång, under perioden 2021-2023, omfattande totalt 25 miljoner svenska kronor.
UNDP kommer vara Sidas avtalspartner.

With a long-standing presence in Palestine, UNDP has a deep understanding of the local context. UNDP enjoys a solid partnership with Palestinian institutions, civil society organizations, and international development partners, as well as the communities themselves.
The Gaza Early Recovery program aims to contribute to restoring safe and unimpeded access to basic services through cash assistance and rubble removal. Through the program, internally displaced non-refugee families will be assisted to find affordable and adequate housing, and at the same time being provided rental subsidies, while awaiting the reconstruction of their destroyed homes. This program will also contribute to creating short-term job opportunities for the economically devastated people in Gaza.
The geographical focus of the contribution will be the whole of the Gaza Strip unless otherwise specified in the agreement.
An eighteen month (18) contribution, covering the period 2021-2023, and amounting to a total of SEK 25 million, is proposed.
UNDP will be Sida’s agreement partner.

The program has responded to three different hostilities in the Gaza Strip; 10-21 May 2021 and 5-7 August 2022 and 9-13 May 2023. It has adopted a comprehensive approach towards the affected populations. The intervention both targeted households with cash packages to obtain decent shelters and provided opportunities to access short-term jobs, to help restore and stabilize their livelihoods.
UNDP has presented results for outputs 3, 4 and 5. Activities under output 1 and 2 were completed 2021 and 2022.
Output 3 Internally displaced refugee and non-refugee households, whose homes were rendered uninhabitable have received Temporary Shelter Cash Assistance (TSCA)
UNDP has, in coordination with the shelter cluster, done a careful selection of beneficiaries to avoid duplication. Beneficiaries have been households with totally damaged or severely damaged housing units, that have not been compensated for rehabilitation from any other funds. Special attention has been given to protection for women.
The program has rapidly responded to the urgent needs of the population in order to restore access to safe shelters. The TSCA support has been provided in three-months intervals. The number of non-refugee households receiving TSCA has gradually decreased over time, from 399 in July 2021 to 40 in September 2023, as some of the targeted housing units were either rehabilitated or reconstructed. In addition to the TCSA UNDP has provided a re-integration package to 339 Households affected by May 2021 hostilities, in addition to 36 non-refugee households affected by August 2022 hostilities. This was a one-time lump sum payment of 500 USD, to enable them to provide the urgently needed non-food items, like housing equipment and supplies, to help displaced families get back on their feet.
In phase 2 of funding for the TSCA UNDP has included the refugee population directly served by UNRWA. This support has been given to refugee families who were displaced from their shelters during May 2021 and August 2022 hostilities and whose housing units have not been reconstructed. 639 refugee eligible families were supported by TCSA between January 2022 to April 2022, which was less than planned. Savings were used to prolong the support.
UNDP's assessment is that the TSCA approach has contributed to ensuring safe living conditions for displaced families and strengthened their recovery and resilience, as they are suffering from the dire economic situation exacerbated by the hostilities.
Output 4: Immediate partial Rehabilitation is conducted for several partially damaged housing for internally displaced non-refugee households and vulnerable households
Activities under this output have addressed rehabilitation of 102 severely damaged housing units of non-refugee internally displaced families due to the May 2021 hostilities. As a result, 628 people - 346 males and 282 females, safely returned to their homes. This has contributed to decreasing the reliance on TCSA. The rehabilitation was implemented through a self-help modality, where the beneficiaries carried out the rehabilitation activities by direct contracting or doing it themselves, in case they had construction experience. Following a second amendment between Sida and UNDP a total of 25 non-refugee households affected by May 2021 hostilities, in addition to 22 non-refugee household affected by August 2022 were supported to rehabilitate their severely damaged housing units, in addition to the rehabilitation of Palestine Tower in Gaza hosting both residents and media offices.
Output 5: People directly affected by the hostilities are provided with dignified short-term job opportunities
In parallel with the assistance for shelter, the project contributed to rapidly securing temporary income for the affected households. UNDP partnered with three implementing partners; the Palestinian Employment Fund, the Palestinian Federation of Industries and the Islamic University of Gaza - Business Technological Incubator.
The project provided short-term job opportunities to 786 beneficiaries who were affected by May 2021 and 2022 hostilities; 325 women and 461 men and 7 % of them are persons with disabilities. This restored and stabilized their livelihoods. 181 persons, of which 122 were youth, have received essential freelancing and soft skills coaching. This empowered them to effectively compete on online freelancing platforms. These activities were completed by August 2023.
An online survey indicates that 77% of the respondents reported significant improvement of their current livelihood. The positive effect was higher in case of women, at 80,7% compared to men at 68,1%. They believed that the short-term opportunity will help them find a more stable opportunity.
Results achieved in 2024 quoted from the Conclusion on Performance 2025: In 2024, Sida agreed with UNDP for reallocated project savings under Output 5, as outlined in the third amendment signed on 13 March 2024, to support solid waste collection efforts with a total allocation of USD 740,348.43. This support enabled the deployment of 285 affected individuals, including sixty-four professionals and skilled graduates, 109 skilled workers and 112 unskilled workers. These individuals contributed to emergency response efforts across the Gaza Strip through the Solid Waste Joint Services Council. The deployment target was fully achieved, with 285 beneficiaries (31 women and 254 men) actively supporting emergency operations during the war in 2024. Their contributions included solid waste collection and disposal, maintenance of water wells serving displacement shelters, winterization support, including rainwater drain cleaning, cleaning of shelters and surrounding areas, cleaning around hospitals, medical points, and public markets.
Examples of achieved results:
The project was able to adopt comprehensive nexus approach towards the affected targeted population. The intervention not only targeted House Holds (HHs) with cash packages to obtain decent and dignified shelters but also ensured that Gazans, directly affected by the latest conflicts, are provided with opportunities to access dignified short-term jobs, to help restore and stabilize their livelihoods. Minor shelter rehabilitation was added as an objective which had a positive effect in reducing the support for rental subsides.
Main results achieved:
Output 2: Concrete rubble and nonconcrete debris safely removed and transported to landfill or crushing site for reuse in rehabilitation activities. The project approach was based on implementing the project activities safely, with guidance from United Nations Mine Action Services (UNMAS), in coordination with the relevant stakeholders. All rubble removal efforts had been completed by the end of June 2022 through which 483 damaged buildings were cleared and a total of 113,000 tons of rubble and debris were safely removed. The project contributed to improving the safety and wellbeing of a total of 50,000 beneficiaries, by rehabilitating 28 roads with the crushed rubble is being used as base coarse in the targeted areas of Gaza. Such intervention had facilitated the movement of residents and other people using these roads as well as the movement of commodities that are needed to support different communities.
Output 3: Internally displaced refugee and nonrefugee households, whose homes were rendered uninhabitable have received Temporary Shelter Cash Assistance (TSCA). The project has rapidly responded to the urgent needs of the population in order to restore access to safe shelters for the internally displaced people (IDPs). 120 nonrefugee households (HHs) out of the initial 399 HHs received TSCA support during the 12 months of 2023. In addition, 110 refugee households (HHs), received TSCA during 2023. Based on an agreement amendment with extra financial contribution from Sida, the original plan with UNDP and UNRWA was to support up to 1,000 refugee families affected by the May 2021 hostilities and internally displaced. Only 639 refugee eligible families were supported by TSCA after obtaining approval from Sida on the new targets for the project.
In addition to the TSCA, UNDP provided a reintegration package to 399 HHs affected by May 2021 hostilities, in addition to 36 nonrefugee HHs affected by August 2022 hostilities as a onetime lump sum payment of US$ 500 per family, to enable them to provide the urgently needed nonfood items, including housing equipment and supplies, to help displaced families get back on their feet. Overall, the TSCA approach contributed to ensuring safe living conditions for displaced families and strengthening their recovery and resilience, as they are suffering from the dire economic situation exacerbated by the hostilities.
Output 4: Immediate partial rehabilitation is conducted for several and partially damaged housing for internally displaced nonrefugee households and vulnerable households (female headed households and those with persons with disabilities). This output, in addition to the support from the Government of Sweden, was partially funded by the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) with a total budget of US$ 1 M. A total of 102 severely damaged housing units of nonrefugee internally displaced families due to the May 2021 hostilities were rehabilitated. As a result, 628 IDPs (346 males and 282 females), including 12 PwDs safely returned to their homes. This has contributed to decreasing the reliance on TSCA. The rehabilitation was implemented through the self-help modality, where the beneficiaries conducted the rehabilitation activities by direct contracting or did it by themselves in case they have construction experience. This methodology is quick and gives the beneficiaries flexibility to meet their various aspirations for the reconstruction of their own homes. By early 2023, UNDP has signed contracts with 23 HHs 0ut of the originally planned twenty-five nonrefugee HHs that were severely damaged during the 2021 hostilities. The number of HHs later increased by four due to a reassessment of some critical cases. Therefore, UNDP has signed contracts with twenty-seven nonrefugee HHs. Out of those, 23 HHs completed the rehabilitation of their damaged houses, while four families were in the final stage of completing the rehabilitation of their houses. Furthermore, out of the originally planned twenty-two nonrefugee HHs that were severely damaged during the 2022 hostilities, and after cross checking with UNRWA, two of them were considered refugees and thus removed from the nonrefugee lists.
Output 5: People directly affected by the hostilities are provided with dignified short term job opportunities. In parallel with the assistance dedicated for the shelter of affected population, the project contributed to rapidly securing temporary income for the affected and vulnerable HHs in the Gaza Strip. This output was achieved through the implementation of two main activities: Deploying 1,036 graduated, skilled, and unskilled workers in the private sector and basic services. Providing 120 graduates with the opportunity to access online jobs by developing their technical and freelancing skills.
Before the end of the project, war on Gaza erupted in October 2023 and it has been ongoing until now bringing about unprecedented destruction and loss in human lives, with at least 54,000 Palestinians killed (out of which around 54.6% are children, women, and elderly), over 115,688 more injured and thousands more still missing under the rubble. At least 1.9 million people in the Gaza Strip (90% of the entire population) have become internally displaced, seeking refuge in overcrowded shelters and unsanitary makeshift camps. The ongoing war has caused largescale and unprecedented destruction of essential public and social infrastructure, resulting in at least fifty million tons of debris as estimated by UNEP and UNOSAT. More than 90% of municipalities have been facing either complete cessation or severe disruption of service provision, across various municipal services. Moreover, the war has resulted in the collapse of solid waste management evidenced by the unprecedented accumulation of solid waste in the streets and the proliferation of unregulated temporary dumping sites, acting as breeding ground for disease vectors and further exacerbating the already alarming public health crisis.
In response, UNDP and Sida have reallocated savings from the project budget under Output 5, as outlined in the third amendment signed on March 13, 2024, to support the solid waste collection efforts at a total amount of US$ 740,348.43. The support to emergency efforts includes the deployment of 285 affected beneficiaries comprising sixty-four professional and skilled graduates, 109 skilled workers, and 112 unskilled workers to bolster solid waste collection in all Gaza strip.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
